paper.title: Disrupting ceramide glycosylation prevents adaptive resistance to osimertinib in in vitro and in vivo models of EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
paper.abstract: Acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a major limitation in the treatment of EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Increasing evidence indicates that sphingolipid metabolism remodelling contributes to drug tolerance and resistance in different cancers, including NSCLC. Here, we investigated whether the combination of an inhibitor of glucosylceramide synthase (GCS) with the EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor osimertinib affects the development of resistance in EGFR-mutated NSCLC cells. The GCS inhibitor venglustat significantly reduces the emergence of osimertinib-resistant colonies after long-term exposure to osimertinib in EGFR-mutated NSCLC cell cultures. Combined treatment decreases drug-tolerant persister cell (DTP) survival and prevents regrowth after drug withdrawal. Genetic silencing of UDP-glucose:ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) confirmed the role of GCS in osimertinib tolerance, reducing DTP survival and resistant colony formation. In a xenograft mouse model, the osimertinib-venglustat combination significantly reduces long-term tumour regrowth compared with osimertinib, without signs of toxicity. Untargeted MS lipidomics identified glycosylated ceramides (GlyCer) as major lipid species associated with resistance development. The concentration-dependent reduction in GlyCer upon GCS inhibition parallels decreased resistant colony formation. Further targeted MS analysis identified Gb3/Cer glycosylation ratio (GR) as a key feature associated with osimertinib resistance. A mechanistic relationship between glycosphingolipids and osimertinib resistance is supported by preliminary data showing increased Gb3 C16:0 GR in plasma from osimertinib-treated EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients at tumour progression compared with pre-treatment levels. These findings support the need for further investigation aimed at evaluating the combination of a GCS inhibitor with osimertinib to prevent the insurgence of resistance to first-line treatment of EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients.
